aliases.name: Aptrgangr
aliases.meaning: again-walker, one who walks after death

description.summary: Norse undead creature, an animated corpse with supernatural powers including superhuman strength, increased size, and shape-shifting. Guards treasure in burial mounds and kills intruders.
description.full: The Draugr is a corporeal undead creature from Norse mythology and Icelandic sagas, distinguished from ghosts by its physical, animated body. Characterized by superhuman strength, the ability to increase in size, and a blackish or dark appearance, draugr guard their burial mounds and treasure hoards with jealous ferocity. They possess various supernatural powers including shape-shifting, immunity to normal weapons, driving people mad, and occasionally prophecy. Draugr emit a distinctive smell of decay and can be defeated through beheading, burning, or heroic combat. They retain their personality from life, often displaying greed, violence, and malevolence.

etymology.origin: Old Norse 'draugr', possibly related to 'draugr' meaning 'ghost' or from 'drjúgr' meaning 'lasting'

height.notes: Can increase in size, becoming much larger than in life

features.description: Appears as animated corpse, showing signs of death and decay
Can swell to massive proportions, larger than in life
Skin turns black, blue-black, or deathly pale
Possesses strength far beyond mortal capability
Emits strong odor of decay and death
Eyes may glow or appear supernatural

physical.morphology: Appears as animated corpse with physical body. Can increase dramatically in size and weight. Shows signs of death but remains mobile and dangerous.

abilities.description: Possesses strength far exceeding mortal men
Can swell to enormous size, becoming massive
Can transform into animals or take other forms
Some draugr are immune to normal weapons
Can cause madness or death through supernatural presence
May foretell future events or speak in verse
Some accounts suggest ability to affect weather

behavior.diet: Not applicable (undead, though some accounts suggest blood drinking)
patterns: Guards burial mound and treasure jealously
Retains personality and grudges from life
May haunt those who wronged them in life
Sometimes leaves mound to terrorize living

range.description: Throughout Norse and Scandinavian regions, particularly Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and Denmark during Viking Age and medieval period.

peak_activity_periods.description: Height of draugr beliefs and saga accounts

origins.cultural_roots: Norse beliefs about the dead, improper burial, and the power of greed beyond death. Related to Viking Age burial practices and beliefs about the afterlife.
origins.earliest_accounts: Viking Age oral traditions, later recorded in Icelandic sagas
origins.folklore_connections: Connected to broader Norse beliefs about death, burial, and the supernatural. Related to concepts of the restless dead across cultures.

timeline.significance: Active belief in undead guardians of burial mounds
timeline.source: Archaeological evidence and later saga accounts

timeline.significance: Famous account of Glámr the draugr
Multiple saga accounts of draugr encounters
Draugr beliefs persist but reinterpreted through Christian lens
Draugr in fantasy literature, games (Skyrim), and Norse cultural revival

history.modern_era: Draugr have experienced significant revival in modern popular culture, particularly through video games like Skyrim, fantasy literature, and renewed interest in Norse mythology.

notable_accounts.name: Glámr the Draugr
notable_accounts.description: Shepherd Glámr dies and returns as powerful draugr, terrorizing region until defeated by hero Grettir in famous battle
notable_accounts.significance: Most famous draugr account in saga literature

notable_accounts.name: Hrapp of Hrappsey
notable_accounts.description: Evil man who promises to cause trouble after death, becomes draugr haunting his farm
notable_accounts.significance: Example of personality continuing after death

notable_accounts.name: Thorolf Twist-Foot
notable_accounts.description: Man buried improperly becomes draugr, must be reburied to stop hauntings

traditions: Proper burial rites to prevent draugr creation
Beheading and burning of dangerous dead
Burial with possessions to satisfy the dead
folklore.beliefs: Draugr represent the danger of greed, improper burial, and evil nature continuing beyond death. They enforce proper treatment of the dead.

indigenous.significance: Central to Norse understanding of death and proper burial. Reflects Viking Age beliefs about the power of the dead and importance of proper rites.
indigenous.sensitivity_note: Part of historical Norse cultural heritage, actively studied and preserved in modern Scandinavia.
indigenous.respect_guidelines: Recognize as important historical belief system and cultural tradition. Understand significance to Norse cultural identity.

literature: Norse sagas (Grettis Saga, Eyrbyggja Saga, etc.)
games: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (prominent draugr enemies)

traditional_methods.description: Decapitate the draugr and place head by buttocks
Burn the body to ashes and scatter or bury at sea
Defeat in physical combat by hero of great strength
Move body to proper burial location with correct rites

researchers.contribution: Analysis of draugr in Norse literature and culture
